paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the LORD is in charge of every nation and every power, and that includes the ones that look unbeatable. Egypt had a Pharaoh, a mighty army, hired soldiers and its own gods. And the LORD says He is the One who thrust the warriors down (Jeremiah 46:15) and will punish Amon, Pharaoh and "those who trust in Pharaoh" (Jeremiah 46:25). So the question for you and me is simple: who are we trusting?

Look at how that Pharaoh gets described: "all noise" (Jeremiah 46:17). Lots of volume, nothing behind it. Friend, I have been all noise in my own bakery, and the cookies did not care. Anything you lean on besides the LORD will make a big sound and then let the appointed time pass it by.

Now hear the other half, because the LORD does. To His servant Jacob He says, "do not be afraid, and do not be dismayed" (Jeremiah 46:27). Then He says it again: "do not be afraid, declares the LORD, for I am with you" (Jeremiah 46:28). He promises to save His people and bring them home, and He is honest that He will "discipline you justly" too (Jeremiah 46:28). Fear doesn't get the last word, friend. The LORD who is with you does, and He means to bring you home.
